turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, Hale, and on what basis?
I don't think this is productive.
"Productive." You asked for this meeting, Hale, so answer my question or I'm walking upstairs to the principal's office.
I'm going to go. I have a class in ten minutes.

At 4:25 in the afternoon? Then before you go, tell me who entered that zero and whether anyone heard Owen first. If you walk out of your own meeting, I'm going straight to the principal's office, and I'll be putting all of this in writing.
Email the principal if you want. I'm done here.

"I'm done here." I'm writing that down, along with the fact that you entered a zero without calling me and then walked out when I asked why. I'm going to the principal's office next, and I'll expect that zero withdrawn and an apology in writing.
